parts.title: The teddy bear I could not lose
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was four, my grandfather gave me a brown teddy bear with one ear missing. I called him Mr Button, because he had a red button instead of an eye. I took him everywhere, to the shops, to the beach and even to the dentist.

Once, when I was six, we went on holiday to Spain. At the airport, I put Mr Button down for a moment, and when I looked again, he was gone. I cried so much that my father went to every desk in the building. After an hour, a cleaner appeared with the bear in her hand. I have never been so happy in my life.

As I grew older, Mr Button spent more time on a shelf. At fourteen, I was embarrassed to have him in my room when friends visited, so I put him in a box.

Last month, I found him again while I was moving to a new flat. His red button was still shiny. I put him on my bed, and when my friends came to dinner, none of them laughed. One of them said that she still had her toy rabbit. Now Mr Button sits proudly on the sofa.

questions.prompt: Why was the bear called Mr Button?
options: He had a red button eye
questions.explanation: He had a red button instead of an eye.

options: He was lost at the airport
questions.explanation: He disappeared at the airport.
A cleaner appeared with the bear in her hand.

questions.explanation: At fourteen she was embarrassed when friends visited.

questions.prompt: How did the friends react last month?
questions.explanation: None of them laughed.

parts.title: Toys through the ages
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Children have always played with toys. [1] Archaeologists have found small clay animals and dolls in graves that are four thousand years old.

In the past, most toys were made at home. [2] Fathers carved wooden horses, and mothers made dolls from cloth.

In the nineteenth century, factories began to produce toys in large numbers. [3] Suddenly, even poor families could afford a doll or a spinning top.

Plastic arrived in the 1950s and changed everything. [4] The new toys were cheaper, brighter and almost impossible to break.

Today, many toys use electronics and can talk, move or connect to the internet. [5] Even so, simple things such as wooden blocks and balls remain as popular as ever.
sentences: The oldest ones may have been used in religious ceremonies.
Factories could shape it into any form.
Some experts worry that children play outside less.
Toys have been enjoyed by almost everyone.

gaps.explanation: The oldest toys may have been ceremonial; the next sentence gives finds from graves.
Parents used whatever they had; the next sentence gives fathers carving horses.
Prices dropped; the next sentence says even poor families could afford toys.
Factories could shape plastic into any form; the next sentence says the new toys were cheaper.
Some experts worry about outdoor play; the next sentence says simple toys remain popular.

parts.title: A letter to a toy company
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to complain [1] a toy that I bought for my son last week. The box said that it was suitable [2] children aged five, but the pieces are far too small. My son is five, and he [3] open the box without help. Worse still, one part [4] after only two days. I would like to [5] my money back, or I would like a new toy. I am sorry to bother you, but I am sure you [6] understand my problem. Yours faithfully, Mrs Hayden

questions.explanation: We complain about something we bought.
Suitable for children is the correct pattern.
Could not shows he was not able to open it.
Broke is the past tense for something that happened.
Have my money back is the pattern after would like to.
I am sure you will understand: future prediction.

parts.title: The toy exchange
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Every year, our town holds a toy exchange. Children bring old toys that they do not play with any more [1] swap them for different ones. It is a clever idea, because nothing is wasted, and nobody spends a penny. This year, more than two hundred children came, [2] the hall was full of games, dolls and books. A girl called Moss swapped her bicycle helmet [3] a puzzle with five hundred pieces. She said that she had never had one before. Some children arrived early to make sure that they [4] the best toys. The organisers think that next year they will need a bigger hall, [5] the event is becoming so popular. Anyone can take part, [6] long as the toys are clean and not broken.

gaps.explanation: Bring toys to swap them: purpose.
More than two hundred children came, so the hall was full.
Make sure they got the best toys.
Because gives the reason: the event is becoming popular.
As long as means on condition that.

parts.title: A talk by a toy museum guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the Toy Museum. I am Dov, and I will be showing you around today. The museum opened in nineteen ninety, when a local man gave us his collection of five hundred toys. Today we have more than six thousand. Our oldest object is a wooden horse from eighteen hundred. On the first floor, you will find dolls from different countries, and on the second floor, there are model trains. Children can play in the activity room, which is open from ten until three. Our shop sells postcards, puzzles and small wooden animals. Everything in the shop is made in this country. Please do not touch the toys in the glass cases, but you may take photos, as long as you do not use the flash.

gaps.explanation: She says the museum opened in nineteen ninety.

gaps.prompt: The museum now has more than ___ toys
gaps.explanation: She says there are more than six thousand toys.

gaps.prompt: The oldest object is a wooden ___
gaps.explanation: She says the oldest object is a wooden horse.

gaps.prompt: The model trains are on the ___ floor
gaps.explanation: She says there are model trains on the second floor.
She says it is open from ten until three.

gaps.prompt: Visitors must not use the ___ for photos
gaps.explanation: She says do not use the flash.

parts.title: An interview with a toy designer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Holt, you design toys for children. How do you get your ideas?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I watch children play. They always do the unexpected. Once, a boy turned a cardboard box into a spaceship, and I thought, why not sell a box?

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Did you?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Almost. We made a box with simple lines to draw on. It became our best seller, and it was very cheap.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What makes a good toy?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It must be safe, of course, but also simple. The best toys let children use their imagination. A stick can be a sword, a horse or a magic wand.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How long does it take to produce a new toy?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: About eighteen months. We test every toy with children aged three to eight, and they are the toughest judges.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do they say?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Honestly, things like, this is boring. Then I go back to my desk and start again.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was your favourite toy as a boy?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A wooden train that my father made. I still have it in my office.
